clue.text: Tied lace in a knot, being fastidious

definitions.note: the definition includes 'being', so it reads as an adjective phrase

indicators.note: lace tied in a knot is twisted out of shape, so the letters of the two words are tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone fussy insists on tying their shoelaces into a neat knot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a knot' signals an anagram of TIED LACE, all eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A delicate person is fussy and easily offended, much like a fastidious one.

clue.text: Sound fruit sinks

indicators.note: placed first, this word tells the solver to say the next word's synonym out loud and spell what is heard

parts.note: a drupe is a stone fruit such as a plum or cherry

explanation.surface: Ripe, healthy fruit goes to the bottom of the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective meaning healthy, but it is the homophone signal: DRUPES is said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To droop is to sag or sink downward, as a wilting flower does.

clue.text: The refuse issue

definitions.meaning: rubbish dropped and left lying about
offspring, a brood of young born together

explanation.surface: A council official raises the matter of rubbish collection.
explanation.definitionFit: Litter is both scattered rubbish and the young a mother animal bears at one birth.

clue.text: A number edge in, almost all delinquent

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
a rim is the edge of a cup or wheel

indicators.note: almost the whole word means the final letter of 'all' is dropped

explanation.surface: Most youngsters edging into trouble are reckoned to be delinquent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter of ALL to give AL.
explanation.definitionFit: A delinquent, as a noun or adjective, is someone breaking the law, a lawbreaker.

clue.text: Building site restrictions

indicators.note: building something means putting it together, so the letters of site are assembled into a new word

explanation.surface: Construction sites come with plenty of rules and limits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Building' signals an anagram of SITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ties are bonds or obligations that restrict one's freedom.

clue.text: Minister about to call back to present an ultimatum

indicators.note: about means going round, so the two letters of the minister surround the rest

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a degree held by many clergy

indicators.note: back tells the solver to read the word for call in the reverse direction

parts.note: to call someone something is to name them

explanation.surface: A government minister is about to recall someone and issue a final warning.
explanation.walkthrough: DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a degree many clergy hold, which is why it can stand for a minister; 'to call' should not be taken as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To insist firmly on something, leaving no room to refuse, is to give an ultimatum.

clue.text: 31 left in oriental country

parts.note: E stands for east, the oriental direction
a state is a nation or country

explanation.surface: A piece of land left behind in an Eastern nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 31 is the answer to 31 across, PROPERTY: the possessions someone leaves when they die are their estate.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead person's estate is all the possessions and assets they leave behind.

clue.text: Friendly understanding of everybody with a nice disposition

parts.note: all means everybody

indicators.note: a disposition is an arrangement, so the letters of a nice are set out anew

explanation.surface: Getting on well with everyone comes from having a pleasant temperament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposition' looks like temperament but signals an anagram of A NICE, giving IANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: An alliance is a pact or union formed on cordial terms between parties.

clue.text: A gift for the fellow no-one thanks on retirement

parts.note: a don is a college fellow at a university

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing, going back, so the letters run in reverse order

parts.note: no, followed by one written as the Roman numeral I
ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: A college fellow is given a retirement present that no one thanks him for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on retirement' turns NOITA into ATION, which follows DON.
explanation.definitionFit: A donation is something given freely, a contribution or present.

clue.text: Generally described as striking and wrinkled

parts.note: workers on strike are out
a lined face is wrinkled

explanation.surface: A face sketched as remarkable and creased with age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striking' looks like an adjective meaning impressive, but it gives OUT, as in workers out on strike.
explanation.definitionFit: To outline is to describe in broad terms, giving only the main points.

clue.text: Wrap a quarter taken surreptitiously

parts.note: a stole is a shawl or wrap worn round the shoulders
N, north, is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: A thief quietly makes off with a quarter of a shawl.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stolen has been taken by theft, slipped away without permission.

clue.text: The doctor is very young — and so wet!

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor
aged ten is very young

explanation.surface: A doctor so youthful is still damp behind the ears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wet' is a verb here, so it matches the verb answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To moisten is to dampen, to make slightly damp.

clue.text: Prices can vary, that's the conspectus

indicators.note: something that can vary may change, so the letters of prices are changed round

explanation.surface: A summary admits that costs can fluctuate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can vary' signals an anagram of PRICES.
explanation.definitionFit: A conspectus is a summary or overview, an abstract of a text.

clue.text: Not favouring a brochure offering a bargain

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
a tract is a pamphlet or small booklet

explanation.surface: A leaflet advertising a special deal is greeted with scepticism.
explanation.definitionFit: A bargain in its old sense is an agreement struck between two parties, a deal.

clue.text: Appeal to a man on the wagon holding up transport

indicators.note: holding means keeping something inside, so the teetotal letters enclose the rest

parts.note: someone on the wagon has given up drink, so is TT, teetotal

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up reads a word from bottom to top, in reverse

parts.note: a cart is a simple means of transport

explanation.surface: A request is made to a sober man who is delaying the traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the wagon' is the idiom for having given up alcohol; 'up' works as a reversal only because this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To attract is to draw in, to be pleasing or interesting to someone.

clue.text: Extremely tense Greek character facing trial

parts.note: tau is the Greek letter T
a test is a trial

explanation.surface: A nervous Greek stands before the court awaiting judgement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' means a letter of the alphabet, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Tautest is the superlative of taut, pulled most tight, like a stretched rope.

clue.text: A nymph's city house

parts.note: EC is the postcode area of the City of London

explanation.surface: A mythical spirit owns a property in town.
explanation.walkthrough: EC, the postcode of London's financial district, is a common crossword City.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Echo is a mountain nymph who could only repeat the words of others.

clue.text: Courageous, having been at the whisky bottle?

definitions.text: having been at the whisky bottle?
definitions.meaning: humorously, filled with spirits after drinking whisky

explanation.surface: Someone acting bravely may have had a drink or two for Dutch courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirited means lively and bold; the second sense jokes about spirit as distilled alcohol.

clue.text: Backing down would be soft!

explanation.surface: Retreating from a position would show weakness.
explanation.definitionFit: Yielding is both conceding ground in an argument and being pliant under pressure.

clue.text: Strike over some rising hot air

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the first word above the second in the grid

parts.note: to clap is to strike, as hands together

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising reads a word from bottom to top, in reverse

parts.note: part means some, a portion

explanation.surface: Industrial action over a rising heat wave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns PART into TRAP, placed under CLAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Claptrap is empty, pretentious talk, nonsense spouted to win applause.

clue.text: Quietly give support when settled

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical instruction to play quietly
to aid is to help or support

explanation.surface: A discreet helper lends a hand once things calm down.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill that is paid has been settled, the debt cleared.

clue.text: Businesslike hospital attendant

definitions.meaning: a hospital worker who does non-medical tasks such as moving patients

explanation.surface: A hospital porter goes about tasks efficiently.
explanation.definitionFit: Orderly means tidy and methodical, and is also the name for a hospital ancillary worker.

clue.text: Make out the guy is on time

indicators.note: in a down clue, one word being on another places it above in the grid

parts.note: a guy is a man
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone reckons the fellow is punctual.
explanation.definitionFit: To make out, in the sense of get by or cope, is to manage.

clue.text: A falling star can appear remote

indicators.note: the word remote can appear in another form, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shooting star looks very distant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can appear' signals an anagram of REMOTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A meteor is the streak of light seen when space debris burns up in the atmosphere, popularly a shooting star.

clue.text: Cold weather protection for a cow

definitions.meaning: a knitted pullover worn for warmth
a breed of dairy cattle from the Channel Island of the same name

explanation.surface: Keeping a cow warm in winter.
explanation.definitionFit: A jersey is a woolly pullover, and a Jersey is a breed of dairy cow from one of the Channel Islands.

clue.text: Confidence concerning a client short of time, possibly

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: possibly signals the remaining letters may be arranged another way
short of means lacking, so a letter is taken out

explanation.surface: Trust in a customer who is pressed for time may be misplaced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short of' removes T from A CLIENT, leaving ACLIEN; 'possibly' rearranges those letters into LIANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Reliance is trust or dependence placed in someone or something.

clue.text: Providing a snack meal before church for everyone

indicators.note: before places the snack ahead of the church letters

parts.note: a pie can be a snack or a light meal
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A quick bite is laid on for everyone before the church service.
explanation.definitionFit: Apiece means each, to or for each one.

clue.text: A person exercising requires some house-room

indicators.note: some of the letters of house-room are taken, a run inside the phrase

explanation.surface: A gym enthusiast needs plenty of space at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' signals the answer is a run of letters within HOUSE-ROOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is someone who exercises, that is employs, a right or tool.

clue.text: Hearing about second class of people

definitions.note: the definition is a noun phrase, while the answer is an adjective describing such a group

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the hearing goes round the letter

parts.note: a trial is a court hearing
B is second, as in B-grade

explanation.surface: A court hearing concerns a second-rate group of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing' suggests listening, but it is a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: Tribal describes a tribe, a group or kin of people sharing ancestry and customs.

clue.text: They'll take pursuers all over the place

indicators.note: something all over the place is scattered in disorder, so the letters of pursuers are jumbled

explanation.surface: Fugitives lead their chasers everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over the place' signals an anagram of PURSUERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Usurpers are those who seize power or a throne wrongfully.

clue.text: Closely followed with some persistence

explanation.surface: Someone shadowed another stubbornly.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogged is both tailed relentlessly, as a hound follows, and tenacious, unwilling to give up.

clue.text: Quality goods

explanation.surface: High-grade merchandise.
explanation.definitionFit: Property means both an attribute or trait and things owned, possessions.
